objective_for_doctor:
Age: 43
Sex: M
Chief Complaint: symptoms worse when lying down and alleviated while sitting up

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

My symptoms are worse when lying down and better when I’m sitting up. I’m also having significant shortness of breath/difficulty breathing, and I’ve had bouts of choking or shortness of breath that wake me up at night.
Have you noticed any swelling in your legs, ankles, or feet, or have you had any recent unexplained weight gain?
Yes. I have swelling in my body, including my ankles, calves, and tibia (both sides).
Are you currently experiencing any chest pain, pressure, or tightness?

Yes—I have pain related to my reason for consulting, and I’ve also had a heart attack or angina (chest pain). The pain is in the lower chest and sides of the chest (right and left) and in the breast (right and left), with radiating pain to the biceps (left), jaw, scapula (left), triceps (left), and shoulder (right). The pain intensity is 6/10.
Does the chest pain or shortness of breath worsen with physical exertion, or does it primarily occur at rest?
I don’t know. My shortness of breath is significantly worse when I’m lying down and better when I’m sitting up.
[DDX] Acute decompensated heart failure, Acute coronary syndrome, Pulmonary embolism, Pericarditis, Pneumonia
